The blocking dependence is **within-iteration flow**: line 6 updates `u[ju[i]]`, and line 7 reads from `u[ku[i]]` in the same iteration. If `ju[i] == ku[i]`, iteration i reads the value line 6 just wrote. Additionally, **between-iteration flow** is possible: if `ju[i] == ku[j]` for i < j, iteration j reads a value updated by iteration i.

Solution: decouple by accumulating updates into temporary buffers (`u_updates`, `v_updates`) during the main loop, then merge them back. This removes all intra-loop dependencies—`u` and `v` are read-only inside the loop—exposing the second loop as a Do-All (or Reduction, if index arrays have collisions) parallelizable pattern. Output is preserved: the same elements receive the same cumulative contributions, just accumulated separately before merge.
